chunks.excerpt: There are residential homes all around the city. There are also lots of 3-star hotels with very affordable prices. In the city there's only one camping site (Prelada), but it's a bit far from the centre. There aren't many family houses to rent in Porto, so they'll be difficult to find.

chunks.title: Porto
chunks.attribution: Content from Wikivoyage is licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.
chunks.excerpt: There are a few companies providing door-to-door shared shuttle service to Porto.  It is a budget option with more personal service than the bus. You can get to Porto from Lisbon with Daytrip shared shuttle or from Coimbra with Coimbra airport shuttle. Prices start at €53, and tickets can be booked in advance to guarantee a seat.

chunks.title: Porto
chunks.attribution: Content from Wikivoyage is licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.
chunks.excerpt:
There may be pickpockets in heavily crowded areas and on public buses and trains; however, pickpocketing is not common in Porto. Travelling by bus or metro is generally safe and one of the best ways to go from a place to another.
Porto is generally a safe place to be if you take normal precautions like walking in well-illuminated streets at night.
